routes.name: General work permit (Employment of Non-Citizens Act 2007)

note: Papua New Guinea, read on 2026-10-30 in Business Advantage PNG's guide to work permits (an online business magazine; secondary, written by the managing directors of two PNG employment consultancies, summarising the Employment of Non-Citizens Act 2007). Every non-citizen seeking employment needs a valid work permit, granted by the Secretary of the Department of Labour and Industrial Relations (DLIR) under the Act, before starting work; the general work permit is for commercial employment (a volunteer permit is for unpaid work, not written). Permits are non-transferable, issued for a specific person, employer and job, any change needing a new permit (work: the sponsor's). Short-term permits last up to six months and aren't renewable; long-term permits up to three years, or five for an employer designated a Good Corporate Citizen; a long-term permit is renewed for the same position with the same company, applied for three months before expiry (renewable; no term written, the years being maxima). An applicant without a valid work permit must apply from outside PNG, through a registered employment agent lodging at DLIR (so `apply` is left out: abroad for a first permit, in the country for a renewal). The Department usually decides within 15 working days of lodgement with correct papers (written as the time; the guide says 'usually'). Its fee isn't given. The entry permit (visa) the Immigration and Citizenship Authority issues alongside isn't described, and ica.gov.pg answered 403 to this research client; the Act itself on PacLII sits behind a bot check.

sources.title: Business Advantage PNG: Work permits in Papua New Guinea
sources.said: All non-citizens who seek employment in PNG must possess a valid work permit before they can commence employment. The work permit must be granted by the Secretary, DLIR, in accordance with the Employment of Non-Citizens Act 2007 . ... A general work permit for commercial employment ... Short-term work permits are valid for up to six months and are non-renewable. Long-term work permits can last for up to three years, or five if the employer is designated a Good Corporate Citizen under the Act. ... Work Permits are non-transferable; that is they are issued for: a specific person, a specific employer, and a specific job. ... If the applicant does not hold a valid work permit, the applicant must apply from outside of PNG. ... the Department will usually process a work permit application within 15 working days from date of lodgement. ... Existing work permit holders are required to apply for a renewal of their work permit three (3) months prior to its expiring. A renewal only applies if the application is for the same position in the same company.
